name: OpenClaw

surfaces.label: Gateway as launchd runs it: node .../openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 18789 (WebSocket + HTTP on 127.0.0.1:18789, LaunchAgent ai.openclaw.gateway). Runs every turn for every channel, cron and heartbeat. In 2026.4.29 the foreground-gateway fast path (dist/cli/run-main.js tryRunGatewayRunFastPath) builds a bare commander program with no preAction hook, so this process is never retitled and ps keeps the full argument string. A gateway started from a terminal with `openclaw gateway` is titled just `openclaw` (dist/entry.js) and cannot be matched by name.

openclaw tui (its aliases terminal and chat run the same command and are titled openclaw-tui) or one-shot openclaw agent: clients of the gateway. tui --local and agent --local run the agent loop in their own process. openclaw agent lives for one turn only.
openclaw acp: ACP stdio bridge that an IDE launches; forwards prompts to the gateway

openclaw node run: headless node host that lets a remote gateway run system.run and canvas on this Mac. Every `openclaw node <subcommand>` (status, install, start, stop...) is also titled openclaw-node for its short life, so a short-lived status call looks like a node host.

OpenClaw.app menu bar companion (optional; owns TCC permissions, attaches to the launchd gateway). Recognise by bundle id only: it never runs turns, so it carries no process spec and is never classified.

working_signals.name: caffeinate
working_signals.meaning: Only when the agent runtime is claude-cli (the default for this install): the gateway keeps a long-lived `claude` stdio child per session and that Claude Code should hold a caffeinate for the length of each turn. Inferred from the claude-code row plus OpenClaw source; never observed for a claude -p stream-json child, and the gateway is not running on this Mac. Does not fire for the built-in pi runtime, which runs in-process.

Valid for the installed 2026.4.29 only: any ~/.openclaw/agents/*/sessions/*.jsonl or *.trajectory.jsonl modified in the last 20 s means the gateway has a turn in flight. One gateway serves all sessions, so this cannot be attributed to a process, only to the gateway. Precise form of the same fact: a <session>.jsonl.lock file exists whose JSON pid is alive (session write lock, held for the whole run, deleted at the end). Current upstream docs (fetched 2026-09-29) say runtime session rows, transcripts and trajectory events moved to ~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite and the lock became a durable activeWriterRunId claim, so on newer releases neither the jsonl mtime nor the .lock file will exist; this signal is then silent and only tree_cpu remains.
Gateway process tree CPU. Weak: the gateway also burns CPU on channel I/O, so use only as a fallback.

waiting_signals.meaning: Gateway broadcasts this WebSocket event to operator clients (Control UI, macOS app) when a tool call needs a human decision; exec.approval.resolved ends it. Also plugin.approval.* for plugin approval flows. `exec.approval.list` lists pending ones. Cannot happen on this install: exec-approvals ask is off.

Approval prompts and questions are delivered as chat messages on the channel (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp...), so the human may be waiting on a phone, not a terminal. No process-level or file-level waiting signal exists.

hooks.config: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json under hooks.internal (enable with `openclaw hooks enable <name>`); hook dirs: bundled, plugin, ~/.openclaw/hooks/, <workspace>/hooks/ (each a directory with HOOK.md + handler.ts). Typed plugin hooks are registered in code by plugins, not in config.

telemetry.how: Bundled diagnostics-otel plugin, OTLP/HTTP protobuf only (grpc ignored), off by default: plugins.allow + plugins.entries.diagnostics-otel.enabled=true and diagnostics.otel.enabled=true with endpoint (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT). Exports metrics (openclaw.session.state, openclaw.run.duration_ms, openclaw.queue.depth, openclaw.tokens), traces (openclaw.run, openclaw.model.call, tool exec) and logs. Content capture is opt-in per key. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/opentelemetry

sources.claim: Process title: setProcessTitleForCommand sets process.title = '<cli>-<top-level command name>' in the commander preAction hook, but the launchd gateway command (`gateway --port 18789`) never reaches that hook. dist/cli/run-main.js tryRunGatewayRunFastPath builds a bare Command with only the gateway/run subcommands, and isGatewayRunFastPathArgv accepts `gateway`, `gateway run` and the run flags (--port, --bind, --token, --verbose...). So the real daemon keeps its full node args and is NOT titled openclaw-gateway; only non-run subcommands (gateway status, health, call, install...) are. dist/entry.js:274 sets process.title = 'openclaw' for anything started through openclaw.mjs (for example `openclaw gateway` typed in a terminal), and for non-gateway commands entry.js respawns a node child, so a client appears as a parent titled openclaw plus a child titled openclaw-<command>. tui aliases terminal and chat have name() = tui, so openclaw-terminal and openclaw-chat never occur
sources.evidence: dist/program-BrS1V7cf.js:46 (setProcessTitleForCommand, registered only in buildProgram at line 108); dist/cli/run-main.js:118-175 (fast path) and :341-366 (buildProgram only after the fast path and route decline); dist/entry.js:274 and :~160-215 (respawn plan, skipped for foreground gateway run); dist/tui-cli-DcNLae-q.js:7 program.command("tui").alias("terminal").alias("chat"). Executed consumeGatewayRunOptionToken from dist/command-path-policy-CYON1JVG.js: ['--port','18789'] -> 2, ['status'] -> 0. Commander test with the installed package: preAction sees name 'tui' for tui, terminal and chat. Only two process.title assignments exist in dist (grep). Not observed on a live gateway: it was not running

sources.claim: On macOS a Node process.title assignment replaces the whole `ps args` string (arguments become invisible), so a retitled openclaw client (openclaw-tui, openclaw-acp, openclaw-node, or the bare openclaw parent) loses its argv, and only the un-retitled gateway keeps its args
sources.evidence: `node -e "process.title='openclaw-gateway'; console.log(require('child_process').execSync('ps -p '+process.pid+' -o args=').toString())"` printed 'openclaw-gateway' and nothing else. Reproduced 2026-09-29 by the verifier with nvm node v22.22.2: ps showed 'openclaw-gateway' only, and agents_probe --row matched that fake process as a daemon (so the name is spoofable and any process titled that way matches). Emulation only, no real OpenClaw process was running

sources.claim: Installed 2026.4.29 stores sessions as ~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/sessions/sessions.json plus <sessionId>.jsonl; state is owned by the gateway, so a transcript cannot be mapped from a process because one gateway serves all sessions. Current upstream docs no longer say this: they put runtime rows and transcripts in ~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite and call sessions.json the legacy migration source
sources.evidence: ls -la ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions (2026-09-29): <uuid>.jsonl, <uuid>.trajectory.jsonl, <uuid>.trajectory-path.json, sessions.json. Local docs of 2026.4.29 (docs/concepts/session.md) say jsonl. https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/session ('Where state lives', fetched 2026-09-29) now says SQLite, so this URL no longer supports the jsonl store

sources.claim: Transcript record shape (2026.4.29): <session>.jsonl header line has keys cwd,id,timestamp,type,version (type 'session'); later lines are type message (keys id,parentId,timestamp,message) or thinking_level_change. Trajectory sidecar lines have keys data,modelApi,modelId,provider,runId,schemaVersion,seq,sessionId,sessionKey,source,sourceSeq,traceId,traceSchema,ts,type,workspaceDir with types session.started, trace.metadata, context.compiled, prompt.submitted, model.fallback_step, model.completed, trace.artifacts, session.ended. sessions.json is a dict keyed by session key (agent:main:main) whose row carries status, startedAt, endedAt, updatedAt, runtimeMs, abortedLastRun, sessionFile, sessionId, claudeCliSessionId, cliSessionIds, cliSessionBindings, lastInteractionAt, sessionStartedAt
sources.evidence: python json key listing of one record of each file under ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions, re-run 2026-09-29 (key names and type values only, no content read); event names match https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/trajectory, which now says live capture goes to SQLite and .trajectory.jsonl files are legacy

sources.claim: A per-session write lock file <session>.jsonl.lock exists for the duration of a run in 2026.4.29; it stores pid and createdAt (and starttime) and is treated as stale if the pid is dead or recycled. Current upstream replaced it with a durable activeWriterRunId claim in SQLite

sources.claim: Turns start with no human present: heartbeat runs a main-session turn on a timer, and cron jobs and channel messages start turns too. Docs say the default is 30m, or 1h when Anthropic OAuth/token auth (including Claude CLI reuse) is detected and heartbeat.every is unset. On this Mac gateway.log holds 3474 'trigger=heartbeat' cli exec lines and 2 'trigger=user' between 2026-05-02 and 2026-07-24, at about 30 minute spacing (12:15, 12:45, 13:15 on 2026-05-02), so the observed cadence here is 30m, not 1h

notes: One gateway process serves every session, so a process cannot be mapped to one transcript: report working/idle for the gateway as a whole and list session rows from sessions.json (status running/done/failed/timeout, updatedAt). Scope: process patterns, session store and lock claims are for the installed 2026.4.29; upstream (2026.7.x and later) moved sessions to SQLite and changed the lock, and has not been checked for process titles. No real OpenClaw process was observed running, so nothing here is verified-locally. Recognising the gateway: on 2026.4.29 the launchd daemon is `node .../openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 18789` with full args (never retitled). A gateway typed in a terminal as `openclaw gateway` shows the bare title `openclaw` and is not matched (a bare `openclaw` is also the wrapper parent of every respawned client, so matching it would be wrong); confirm a gateway by the listener on 18789 (lsof). `openclaw-gateway` is NOT matched on purpose: on 2026.4.29 it appears only on short-lived `openclaw gateway status|health|call|install...` runs, never on the daemon. Client processes (tui, acp, node host, macOS app) do not run turns except `tui --local` and `agent --local`. openclaw-node also covers short-lived `openclaw node status|install|...`. Warning: with the default claude-cli runtime the gateway's child is a real `claude` process (args carry --resume <id> when resuming, not --session-id), so the claude-code row will also match it; a detector should drop any claude whose parent is the gateway or it will double count. The waiting state is not observable from disk or ps. Live run 2026-10-01: the terminal-started gateway is invisible to argv matching; find it by the listener on 18789. Its claude child is the thing to count, under the claude-code row, and it can outlive the gateway.
